item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's comment on the evacuation of passengers and crew of the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov from the Spitsbergen archipelago
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's comment on the evacuation of passengers and crew of the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov from the Spitsbergen archipelago (September 8, 2026) 💬 On September 8, a group of passengers and crew members (69 people in total) from the Russian research vessel Professor Molchanov, arrested on September 2 in Spitsbergen at the request of Ukrainian companies, crossed the Russia-Norway border and is now en route to Murmansk. The Russian nationals were evacuated with assistance from the Norwegian authorities through close coordination between State Trust Arktikugol , Embassy of Russia in Oslo and the Russian Consulates General in Spitsbergen and Kirkenes . ☝️ The Russian nationals have received the necessary assistance and support. Following their border crossing, the Murmansk regional authorities are helping arrange their onward journey to Murmansk.

item.title: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov during talks with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud
item.description: 🎙 Opening remarks by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov during talks with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Saudi Arabia Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud (Moscow, September 8, 2026) 💬 Sergey Lavrov: We are pleased to welcome you to Moscow. We highly appreciate that, despite the difficult situation in the region, you found the time to come to Moscow. This underscores the special nature of our relations , which are not dependent on the current political climate and are focused on implementing the agreements reached by our Leaders. We particularly value this visit and the opportunity to hold substantive talks , especially given that this year marks the centenary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Russia and Saudi Arabia . This is a good opportunity to take a detailed look at the state of Russia-Saudi relations. They continue to expand year by year in trade and the economy, investment, culture and humanitarian cooperation. We will also discuss regional affairs. 🤝 Russia is sincerely interested in helping advance efforts to calm the situation , as well as in addressing other regional issues of mutual interest. 🇷🇺 🇸🇦 #RussiaSaudiArabia

📃
Article by Their Excellencies Mr Stanislav Krans and Mr Wang Xiaolong, Ambassadors of Russia and China to New Zealand, “Forged in Pain and Fire: WWII History to Defend”, published on
The NZ Herald’s website
(September 4, 2026)
👉
Read in full
• September 3rd marks the 81st Anniversary of the End of World War II.
The Allies’ victory in World War II laid the foundation of the United Nations
that was established in 1945 with the aims, as stipulated at its Charter, “to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war”.
• Nearly 80 percent of the world’s population were drawn into the fiery orbit of hostilities. As the primary theaters of military operations in Europe and Asia, the Soviet Union and China bore the brunt of World War II. Altogether their casualties accounted for over half of the deaths worldwide. Most losses were among civilians who suffered greatly from the Axis powers’ war crimes.
Lest we forget the Chinese and Soviet people’s sacrifice for the victory as well as the contribution of other Allies, including New Zealand, to crushing Nazism and fascism and fighting for a peaceful future!
• During World War II, Japanese militarists’ war of aggression and innumerable crimes inflicted immense suffering on the people of China, Russia and elsewhere across Asia, resulting in the deaths of tens of millions of innocent people
. 80 years have passed, it is painful to see that Japan has not fully reflected on its past crimes.
Instead, shielded and encouraged by outside forces, it now attempts openly to whitewash its aggression and even to return openly to a militarist path.
• Annually, the respective UN General Assembly resolution – sponsored by Russia and co-sponsored by China and 43 other countries
– is supported by the overwhelming majority of member-states
. Last year, 119 nations voted for this document. Unfortunately,
New Zealand is not among them being in the minority, although Kiwis were actively involved in the fight against Nazism
and won fame on the battlefields of World War II.
• Back in the days of World War II, New Zealand and many other nations were on the right side of the history and their cause was just. Russia and China are determined to
stand firmly on the side of international justice and prepared, together with the peace-loving peoples of all nations, to resolutely uphold the post-war world order for the sake of building a bright future for all mankind
.

🎙
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's
answer to a question
from Andrew Napolitano during an interview with Channel One’s
The Great Game programme
(Moscow, September 8, 2026)
❓
Question: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner recently visited Moscow and met with President of Russia Vladimir Putin. What can you tell us about the outcome of this visit?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
Much of the opening part of these talks
was broadcast on television
: President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
’s remarks, followed by statements from
Steve Witkoff
and
Jared Kushner
. Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov, who took part in the conversation,
later gave a detailed comment
.
In our diplomatic tradition,
we generally limit ourselves to what we have decided to make public
.
I do not want to emulate
those who are now beginning to speculate
about
“what Mr Witkoff and Mr Kushner brought to Moscow and what they subsequently took to Kiev”
. A member of Ukraine's parliament has already said that what they brought back was far worse than what Ukraine had previously rejected.
❗️
There is a great deal of speculation.
As for further diplomatic steps,
the American Side has said nothing
.
The French, however, have already announced that they were there and that the Americans supposedly said that,
following the elections to Russia's State Duma
, direct talks involving the US would definitely resume.
I leave all of this on the conscience of the Élysée Palace
, especially given that it has repeatedly gained notoriety for
less-than-ethical conduct
when it comes to disclosing the substance of telephone and other conversations.
The substance of what was discussed is based – and I can say this with confidence – on
the position President Donald Trump outlined on Ukraine
immediately after returning to the Oval Office.
☝️
First, he said that
any attempts to draw Ukraine into NATO should simply be forgotten.
He recalled that this had been clear long before President Vladimir Putin, that the matter was closed and there was no reason to try to reopen it.
👉
The second element of the US position is
recognition of the realities on the ground.
I would particularly stress that
this is not about territories
.
When we speak of realities,
we are talking about people
who, immediately after
the February 2014 coup
, were branded “subhuman”, “specimen” and terrorists. When they rejected the results of
the illegal coup
, the army, combat aircraft and artillery were deployed against them – something categorically prohibited under international humanitarian law.
They were simply not treated as human beings.
Shortly after being elected president in 2014, Poroshenko said that their children – the children of “real Ukrainians” – would go to clean schools and kindergartens, while the children of those living in Donbass would rot in basements
.
So how do the Europeans intend to return these people to the rule of that regime when they call for restoring the 1991 borders?
Simply to hand the territory over to Nazis? Or do they want to punish these people for wanting to preserve their freedom, their culture and their belonging to the Russian world?
I have spoken about this
many times
.
I would like to stress that
the realities on the ground
, which President Donald Trump and his team recognise – as far as we can judge, they continue to recognise them, just as they did in Alaska –
are realities connected with people
,
with the views they expressed in referendums
: in Crimea, in the Donetsk and Lugansk People’s Republics and, of course, in the Zaporozhye and Kherson regions.
The fact that the Americans proceed from these realities in all their contacts with us, above all in their contacts with President Vladimir Putin, naturally elicits
a positive response from us and strengthens our readiness to continue talking with them
.

item.title: 🇷🇺 Today, September 8, we mark the Day of the Languages of the Peoples of Russia for the first time.
item.description: 🇷🇺 Today, September 8, we mark the Day of the Languages of the Peoples of Russia for the first time. The main goal of the holiday is to preserve and support Russia’s linguistic diversity , promote native languages, and strengthen interethnic harmony and respect for the cultures of all the peoples of our country. Russia fosters more than 150 languages , each of which is an invaluable cultural heritage of the peoples of our nation. *** 🔹 More than 190 peoples live in Russia, each with its own cultural and linguistic traditions. There are more than 270 different languages and dialects in total, which can be divided into several major groups: • Slavic languages. Russian is the state language and the most widely spoken language. • Turkic languages. These include Tatar, Bashkir and Chuvash. • Finno-Ugric languages. These include Mari, Udmurt and Komi. • Caucasian languages. These include Avar, Chechen and Ingush. • Paleoasiatic languages. These include Chukchi and Koryak. 🔹 105 languages are represented in the education system: 24 are used as languages of instruction, while 81 are taught as academic subjects. 🔹 Russian is the state language and the most widely spoken language throughout the country. 🔹 The rarest languages of the peoples of Russia include Itelmen and Copper Island Aleut , each of which has only one competent speaker remaining. Several other languages have fewer than ten speakers , including the Orok language on Sakhalin, Negidal and Udege languages in Khabarovsk Kra

🇺🇳
September 8
marks
the 25th anniversary of the adoption in 2001 of
the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action
, which have become fundamental international legal instruments for combating racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance.
The Russian Federation, which was directly involved in developing these instruments,
consistently reaffirms its commitment to the spirit and letter of these agreements
, aimed at ensuring equality for all and protecting human dignity.
Russia’s consistent support for translating the outcomes of the Durban Conference into action is reflected, among other things, in its
co-sponsorship of the UN General Assembly resolution
“A global call for concrete action for the elimination of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance and the comprehensive implementation of and follow-up to the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action”
, introduced annually by the Group of 77 and China.
☝️
A quarter of a century later, the
Durban Declaration and Programme of Action
are
more relevant and significant than ever
.
The Russian Federation actively draws on these documents in its
flagship UN General Assembly initiative
,
“Combating glorification of Nazism, neo-Nazism and other practices that contribute to fuelling contemporary forms of racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and related intolerance”
.
In particular, the first paragraph of
the Russian resolution
states
:
“Reaffirms the relevant provisions of the Durban Declaration and of the outcome document of the Durban Review Conference, in which States condemned the persistence and resurgence of neo-Nazism, neo-Fascism and violent nationalist ideologies based on racial and national prejudice and stated that those phenomena could never be justified in any instance or in any circumstances”.
❗️
We are compelled to note that certain states are now attempting to revise the fundamental principles enshrined in
the Declaration
.
In this regard, we would like to recall that the destructive practice of imposing the concept of “civilizational exceptionalism”, manifestations of neocolonial revanchism, and any divisions along national, cultural, religious or other lines
serve only to destabilise the framework of international law built over decades
, which has become one of the pillars of global stability and security.
The substance of the Durban process is reflected in Russia’s cooperation agenda with African states. Overcoming the legacy of colonialism, ensuring sovereign equality and developing common approaches to building a fairer,
#MultipolarWorld
are
among the priorities of
the Third Russia-Africa Summit
, scheduled to take place in Moscow on October 28-29.

item.description: ⚡️ Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's comment on the International Day of Journalists’ Solidarity (September 8, 2026) 💬 September 8 marks the International Day of Journalists’ Solidarity. The date was established in 1958 in memory of Czechoslovak anti-fascist journalist Julius Fucik , who was executed by the Nazis in 1943. It serves as a reminder of the importance of freedom of speech and professional journalism, while also drawing attention to the safety of media workers and the need for solidarity and mutual support within the global journalistic community. In practice, under far-fetched pretexts, they have blocked Russian television channels, shut down correspondent offices and expelled journalists. The Kiev regime has launched an outright campaign against Russian journalists reporting truthful, first-hand information. in countries whose leaders routinely proclaim their commitment to press freedom while grandly portraying themselves as a “flourishing garden”.
In practice, under far-fetched pretexts, they have
blocked
Russian television channels,
shut down
correspondent offices and
expelled
journalists.
The Kiev regime has launched an outright campaign against Russian journalists reporting truthful, first-hand information.
At the same time,
the neo-Nazi junta’s openly declared intent to kill civilians
– a category that under international law includes media workers – has drawn not the slightest criticism from its Western patrons.
Terrorist attacks have claimed the lives of
:

Igor Kornelyuk
▪️
Anton Voloshin
▪️
Andrey Stenin
▪️
Anatoly Klyan

Ivan Zuev
Dozens of media workers
have also been wounded
while carrying out their professional duties.
It is deeply troubling that these crimes and acts of repression have failed to elicit an adequate response from the Western media community
. Mainstream outlets in those countries, guided by political expediency and in defiance of the principles of journalistic solidarity,
chose to remain silent
and act as though the issue did not concern them. In doing so, they abandoned professional ethics and the very idea of solidarity among journalists.
Those who nevertheless found the courage to defend Russian media workers or honour the memory of those who died for the truth were met with
a barrage of criticism and accusations
, including from fellow journalists.
***
❗️
We call on the global media community to show solidarity with their Russian colleagues and speak out in their defence against politically motivated repression by Western countries.
For our part, we will continue
to consistently defend the rights
of Russian journalists abroad and
seek justice for crimes
committed against Russian correspondents.

🇺🇳
📆
From September 7 to October 7, Geneva will host
the 63rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council
.
The Session
is expected to address
a broad range of issues
on the international human rights agenda, including:
• protection and promotion of economic, social and cultural rights,
• ensuring the right to development,
• protection of children,
• combating discrimination against women,
• advancing the interests of indigenous peoples,
• preventing the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on the enjoyment of human rights, as well as other thematic issues.
At Russia’s initiative, a high-level thematic discussion will be held to mark the
60th anniversary of the adoption of the International Covenants on Human Rights
.
The Council will adopt
the outcomes of the Universal Periodic Review of the national reports
of Belgium, Denmark, Latvia, Namibia, Niger, Nicaragua, Mozambique, Palau, Paraguay, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Singapore, Somalia, Sierra Leone and Estonia.
At the initiative of the EU, the Council will once again consider
a
politicised and highly confrontational
draft resolution
on the human rights situation in Russia, aimed at extending for another year the mandate of the relevant HRC Special Rapporteur,
Mariana Katzarova
of Bulgaria.
❗️
Russia’s stance on this matter
remains unchanged
: we do not recognise the mandate of this illegitimate special procedure, and any form of interaction with it is unacceptable to us.
The Russian delegation, which will participate in the Session
as an observer
, intends, as before, to make active use of all available opportunities
to overcome confrontation
and
promote a unifying agenda
, as well as
to foster among international partners an understanding of the importance of establishing constructive international dialogue
on the promotion and protection of human rights, with due respect for the national, religious, cultural and historical characteristics of every state.
A number of special side events
will be organised to present Russia’s approaches to the most pressing issues on the session’s agenda to the international community.

item.title: : Government of the Russian Federation On September 8, Russia's Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam, P
item.description: Government of the Russian Federation : 🇷🇺 🇻🇳 On September 8, Russia's Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam, President of Vietnam To Lam held a meeting at the Russian Government House. Russia's Prime Minister stressed that Russia remains committed to deepening trade and economic cooperation with Vietnam and advancing joint projects in energy, transport, industry, agriculture, the digital economy and high technology. 💬 Russia's Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin : I would like to warmly congratulate all citizens of your country on Independence Day, which Vietnam celebrated on September 2. Russia was among the first countries to establish diplomatic relations with Vietnam. We stood shoulder to shoulder during the Vietnamese people’s heroic struggle for freedom and independence and throughout the subsequent period of peaceful nation-building . Russia and Vietnam maintain active interregional ties and continue to expand humanitarian cooperation . The two countries are strengthening cooperation in science, education and tourism . Tourist flows continue to grow year by year, while the geography of direct air links is expanding. #RussiaVietnam
